_meta.purpose: Single status manifest for the Kryptr user docs. Every page's front-matter `status` MUST match this file; the 'What's live today' page renders this manifest at build time. Change status here AND in the page front matter in the same commit.

statuses.live: Available in Kryptr today, within the phase boundaries stated on the page.
statuses.preview: Built and visible in the app, but not fully enabled yet — degrades fail-closed.
statuses.planned: Designed and contract-frozen, but not available yet.

_meta.globalPhase: Phase 1 boundary: signing is dry-run only — nothing is broadcast on-chain yet.

pages.title: What is Kryptr
pages.summary: Security-gated finance for autonomous agents; what you can do in the current phase.

pages.title: Wallet & security model
pages.summary: Keyless by construction, read-only by default, security gate, human-in-the-loop; signing arrives later behind a dedicated signer boundary.

pages.title: Fee transparency
pages.summary: Quote fees and the slippage floor are shown before you approve; launchpad fee schedules freeze at launch (launchpad itself is planned).

pages.title: Balances & history
pages.summary: Read-only balances on Base and Robinhood Chain with honest zeros; every action leaves an auditable gate decision.

pages.title: Swaps & quotes
pages.summary: DEX aggregator integration complete (W7-M3). Read-only quote bound to one intent, gate evaluation, approval — execution stops at the unsigned dry-run boundary in this phase.

pages.title: Orders & kill switch
pages.summary: Limit and DCA orders with frozen lifecycle, oracle triggers, three-mode kill switch; wallet endpoints (W7-M1) enable balance reads and transfer intents.

pages.title: Limitations by phase
pages.summary: What Kryptr cannot do yet — including on-chain execution, which has no live signer.

pages.title: FAQ
pages.summary: Custody, automation authority, dry-run phase, verification claims.

pages.title: Glossary
pages.summary: The frozen vocabulary: intents, gate results, kill-switch modes, order statuses, verification claims.
